facts.statement: Dynamopterus velox is an extinct bird known only from a single large right humerus found in France.
facts.quote: Dynamopterus velox is an extinct prehistoric bird, known from a single large right humerus recovered in France.

facts.statement: The humerus of Dynamopterus velox shares anatomical features with living cuckoos but is much larger.
facts.quote: The humerus shares anatomical features with living cuckoos (though it is much larger).

facts.statement: Dynamopterus velox has been classified in the suborder Cariamae within the order Gruiformes.
facts.quote: It has also been classified in the suborder Cariamae in the Gruiformes.

facts.statement: It is debated whether some fossils previously identified as Dynamopterus tuberculatus actually belong to the newly identified group Perplexicervicidae.
facts.quote: Some fossils once thought to be Dynamopterus tuberculatus may actually belong to Perplexicervicidae, a newly identified group of birds with bumpy neck bones that might have helped protect them from predators.

facts.statement: The genus Dynamopterus belongs to the parent group Idiornithidae.
The genus Dynamopterus lived from the Lutetian to the Chattian stages, between 48.07 and 23.04 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Chattian (48.07 to 23.04 million years ago)
